item.title: Unleashing Creative Potential: A Transformative Journey
item.description:
When I first stepped into the course, I was eager but also uncertain about what lay ahead. As someone from a creative industry I considered myself fairly creative, but I also wonder how creativity look like for other businesses and innovations. Little did I know at that time that it would be a journey beyond the typical creativity, but a transformative journey of self-discovery, challenging my preconceived notions and unlocking new realms of creative potential and problem-solving.

Thinking Beyond Boundaries

This was the first creativity self-test prompt. When I saw the prompt, I stared at it and started to think about what this prompt looks like. After the test when we debriefed with our classmates, I realized that although I achieved certain level of creative fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration, the prompt doesn’t necessarily need to be the main object to diverge from. It could be a part of something bigger than that. It could be an element within a larger concept.

This realization prompted me to explore the importance of thinking beyond boundaries.

Next day in the second self test, I consciously shifted my perspective and tried to think out of the box. However, another challenge emerged. This time the prompt was more abstract, merely just a scribble from someone. The abstract nature of the prompt made it difficult to start.

Luckily, once I generated the first idea, I found it became easier to generate the next ideas. I started to generate more ideas as I progressed. I realized that it is the lack of detail in the abstract prompt that challenged me to add more details and interpretations towards it, fueling a cascade of diverse ideas. This exercise taught me that well-designed, open-ended prompts can significantly enhance creative potential by pushing people to think beyond boundaries to generate their own diverse interpretations hence allowing for a greater range of ideas to emerge.

Embracing Ambiguity, Unlocking Diverse Perspectives

One of the most profound lessons came from the last self-test involving a teddy bear. Initially, I approached the task with the assumption that a teddy bear is inherently a stuffed animal, limiting my creative horizons. However, through discussions with my classmates, I realized that the teddy bear could be a design or prototype made from any material and take any form.

This experience enlightened me to the fact that unconscious assumptions can severely limit creative potential. These assumptions often stem from our past experiences and the norms we have internalized, leading us to make decisions and take actions based on preconceived notions. Recognizing and challenging these assumptions is crucial for fostering creativity and effective problem-solving.

Fostering Creativity in Professional Settings

The insights gained from this course have profound implications for my professional life. Embracing open-ended questions and encouraging diverse interpretations can lead to more insightful responses from customers and clients. By actively seeking out different perspectives and challenging my own assumptions, I can gain a richer and more comprehensive understanding of the human side of the business.

Moreover, by consciously applying the principles of thinking beyond boundaries and embracing ambiguity, I can foster a culture of innovation within my team. Encouraging team members to question initial thoughts, ask “What if?” and “Why not?”, and actively observe and discuss diverse perspectives can unlock new avenues for creative problem-solving and exceptional results.

Continuous Self-Reflection and Growth

This course has been a transformative journey, challenging me to confront my preconceived notions and embrace the power of creative thinking. By cultivating an open mindset, embracing ambiguity, and actively seeking out diverse perspectives, I have unlocked new realms of creative potential that will undoubtedly shape my personal and professional growth.

Eventually, we have to either create, or sell. As I continue on this path, I am reminded of the importance of constant self-reflection and a willingness to challenge my own assumptions. Creativity is not a pre-defined destination but a continuous journey of exploration, where we challenge the prompt and business problems raised at us, reframe them and explore new possibilities.

item.title: 那些为了“精英工作”要付出的额外劳动
item.description:
再不做点儿什么别的事情我可能真的要焦虑症躯体化表现了，于是我决定写下这篇博客。

最近在一次偏头痛发作后接下来的几天一直隐隐头晕，不仔细分辨好像感受不到的那种头晕，每次我试图说服自己是不是想多了但大脑总是知道有哪里不对。

跟朋友聊了聊朋友说，小心，这是大脑在向你发射求救信号。

我现在的生活里只有学习，这是我之前上过这么多年义务教育高等教育都从来没有过的体验。你需要其他的生活，这是self care，她说。我明白身体和大脑的极限在哪里，我每天累了就偷懒睡觉玩手机，但是玩手机是因为我只有这个可以选择，是我逃离眼下生活的唯一机会，除此之外我的其他的生活呢？

工作的时候加班再累晚上也会在被窝里看不动脑的网络小说，周末我也会去健身、学小提琴、和朋友们喝酒。现在回归学生的生活，理应自由的时间更多了，反而我的生活只有学校了。

第一年MBA的学校生活很紧张，每六周就要完成3门课，学习内容密度巨大节奏巨快，每天只要是没有课的时候我就会在图书馆，在图书馆学习复习考试，与此同时还要准备实习招聘。在学校的时候除了上课之外还会小组在一起开会准备案例比赛，要么就是参加各种行业公司的networking活动。有一天我惊讶地发现我竟然已经几个月都没看剧了，连看剧都提不起兴趣了。

在MBA这个项目里，要付出的额外劳动太多了，我常常想。与MBA有关的行业和职能，会有预设好的一套行动准则，公司会预期你会这样找人喝咖啡networking这样回答面试问题，学校也会教你在不同的阶段要讲什么样的话怎样讲话。甚至从开学踏进学校的那一刻起，你未来的时间已经被既定的规则规划好了，要在多久之前和多少人喝咖啡，在什么时候之前练习不同类型面试的技巧，在什么时候之前面试找实习。虽然我上过班求过职熟悉这套规则是什么样的，但还是在MBA里被这套“精英工作”的规则震惊到不由自主地被吸进去了。我们像是挂炉烤鸭，在进炉之前先经历填鸭教学，然后把头发梳成大人模样背好每种networking的说辞和答案，直到最后毕业入职，我们油亮饱满地被挂在展示柜里，成为学校下一年就业报告里漂亮的数字来吸引新一批鸭子入炉。

人生是旷野吗？我带着转行的目的来到MBA，却发现好像并没有太多选择。公司美名其曰做这样那样的面试是因为想了解候选人是怎样思考一件事的，但同时他们又都已经抱着候选人们已经练习好面对这样的面试问题要做怎样的回答的预期。我知道为了面试表现优秀我要背这样的模版回答，面试公司也知道优秀的候选人是要用这样的模版来回答问题的，我们像是对爱情还抱有狂野幻想的相亲对象双方。我们到底为什么要付出这么多额外的劳动？是因为只有这样才能让候选人们觉得得到一份精英工作不易要好好珍惜、让面试者们认为我工作的公司门槛很高筛选过程严密，是因为只有这样双方才能都对这样的“精英工作”赋予更大的价值和认同吗？

今天就先写到这里，我需要去复习明天的课堂测验和准备coffee chat的问题和回答，下次想到了再接着写吧。

item.title: Why Do I Start Blogging Now
item.description:
I always feel that I am not a good writer.

In fact, I feel quite comfortable with this self-perception. I’ve read great works, and I know how talented writers look like. This is probably the main reason I refuse to start writing.

I can never allow myself to produce trash especially when I know what masterpiece looks like.

Despite that, I did start to learn violin a couple years ago. I like to go to classical music concerts and listening to the recordings of those virtuoso soloists, but I also find it fun to spend hours, without realizing, practicing to improve my squeaky sound. I guess the reason why I began to type down this article regardlessly is the same. I feel this inner compulsion to.

Recently when I cleaned up my laptop, I was surprised to stumble upon some scratch I wrote 10 years ago. This is why technology is a double-sided sword. It stays forever. Just as how embarrassed I feel when I read those essays, I probably would have the same reaction when I read this blog 10 years later, probably. That’s why I refused to blog.

How immature and ridiculous my thoughts were would stay in the mass database of internet forever. Seriously, one of my high school writing assignment that was published in my school’s blog is still there with a pretty decent SEO ranking if you put my name and the school there. It’s cringy.

Despite the cringe, they are like the post-it tabs. They do remind me of the flow of mind I had then and small pieces of things happened to me at that time. Reading those cringy essays is like looking at a photo album. They record more than my brain can remember.

I battle myself every time when the idea of starting writing resurfaces. I also know that I can never make it to a better writer if I don’t write anything now and open them to criticism.

Moreover, there are so many bad trashy publications out there blatantly asking people to pay for them. (I am very serious about this rant.) If you are also struggling whether to start writing or blogging, just think about them.

To anyone who feels the same as I did, consider this: part of it in writing is to fulfill your own impulses, while the other part of it is to leave an album for your future self to refresh all the pleasant or cringy but sparkling memories.

And to reconcile with the cringy part, this is how I pacify myself: remember that everyone is born and built differently. Your unique perspective may be helpful to someone who has never explored the subjects you write about. And if you just take a moment–why do you find your old writing cringy-—it’s very likely because you’ve evolved into a better writer since then.
